title: ts-sdk-schema-first-tagged-union-interop-zod-jsonschema
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a schema-first TypeScript SDK workflow that generates strongly-typed tagged union types for structured output, plus small runtime helpers that interoperate with Zod and JSON Schema artifacts. This ticket covers: codegen changes, runtime adapters for streaming and non-streaming responses, ergonomics for exhaustive pattern matching, and example migration docs for downstream apps.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Codegen produces discriminated union types and runtime Type Guards; 2) Generated artifacts include minimal Zod schemas and JSON Schema mappings for validation and downstream tooling; 3) Streaming responses surface partial union payloads with stable incremental types and a small "merge" helper for clients; 4) Runtime helpers are tree-shakeable and documented with TypeScript + example migration guide; 5) Performance regressions <= 5% median latency in SDK hot paths; 6) Unit and integration tests cover generation, runtime validation, and a small end-to-end example using the hosted API.

Approach & notes: We'll adopt a schema-first input (authoritative shape specified in a high-level schema file). The codegen plugin will emit: - a discriminated union TS type (tag property configurable), - Zod schema variants for each branch (optional emission behind a flag), - a compact JSON Schema mapping for consumption by 3rd-party validators. For streaming we will emit a pair of types: PartialStreamEvent<T> and FinalStreamResult<T> along with a small helper mergeStreamEvents(events[]) -> T to reconstruct the final union object. The merge helper will be explicit about required fields to avoid silent data loss.

Trade-offs considered: - Emitting Zod schemas increases bundle size; we will gate emission behind a generateSchemas flag and prioritize tree-shakeable runtime helpers over large generated validators. - Using a runtime discriminator (string tag) is simplest for most customers; we will support custom discriminator keys but default to "type". - Strict runtime validation by default can surprise low-trust workflows; default will be lightweight guards and an opt-in strictValidate(apiResponse) that runs full Zod/JSONSchema checks.

Open decisions: - Should the merge helper prefer last-write semantics or explicit presence checks? (Current plan: explicit presence checks and fail-fast in dev mode.) - How to present streaming partials in the SDK: as async iterable of strongly typed events (preferred) vs callback API. We plan AsyncIterable<T> for parity with other SDK streaming APIs.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement codegen + runtime helpers behind feature flag; 2) Add unit tests and example repo under examples/ts-sdk/schema-first-unions; 3) Dogfood internally with Console's rollout rules UI and one mobile sample app; 4) Gradual public rollout with documentation and migration guide.

Metrics: Track adoption by counting generated-schema-enabled repos, number of runtime validation calls, and any error spikes from strict validation. Performance: run existing SDK microbenchmarks and ensure median token path latency regresses <=5%.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Miguel: Initial spike completed. Prototype can generate TS union types and a naive merge helper. Pushed prototype to github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/214 (draft).

2026-02-23 - Aisha: Design review with PM (Nina) and Design (Leo). Decided the default discriminator key should be 'type' and that generated Zod schemas are behind --emit-zod flag. Action: add feature flag and docs outline.
2026-02-28 - Miguel: Implemented AsyncIterable streaming surface and PartialStreamEvent<T> type. Integration test with hosted API emulator passes for simple two-branch union.

2026-03-03 - QA: Found edge case where merge helper lost optional nested arrays when events arrive out-of-order. Miguel updated merge strategy to do presence-first merging and added deterministic ordering tests.

2026-03-05 - Security review request filed with security team (SEC-1384) to evaluate runtime validation knobs and potential injection vector from user-provided JSONSchema. Security asked for capability flags and docs; marked security_review_required=true in follow-up ticket.

2026-03-08 - Docs: Draft migration guide added at docs/ts-sdk/schema-first-unions.md. Example snippets include: const stream = client.chat.stream({schema:'examples/order.schema.json'}); for-await (const ev of stream) { match(ev, { Order: o => ..., Cancel: c => ... }); }

2026-03-10 - PR feedback: Internal review requested more exhaustive type tests and an example showing Zod strict validation opt-in. Also requested that generated code export both Type Guards (isX) and a runtime-dispatch helper (dispatchUnion).

2026-03-12 - Miguel: Addressed review comments, tightened tests, and updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/214 (ready for final review). Preparing canary dogfood in staging with console rollout rules.
